author: caarlos0
body:
This, in conjunction with #5948, will allow users to read the password of a given `artifactory` or `upload` configuration from a file, example:

```yaml
artifactories:
- password: '{{ readFile "~/.artifactory.txt" }}'
  # ...
uploads:
- password: '{{ readFile "~/.myapi.txt" }}'
  # ...
```

closes #5946

- [x] Followed the steps in the contributor's guide: https://crashoverride.com/docs/other/contributing#filing-the-pull-request
- [x] PR title uses [semantic commit messages](https://nitayneeman.com/posts/understanding-semantic-commit-messages-using-git-and-angular/#fix)
- [x] Filled out the template to a useful degree
- [x] Updated `CHANGELOG.md` if necessary

## Issue

heartbeats/postexec is taking too much memory (>300Mb).

## Description

allow to read elfs only sections we actually need vs reading/parsing the whole file. This brights up regular elf parsing memory utilization to around 60M so for postexec/heartbeats its around 100M locally now

## Testing

```
V reset;
  echo > ~/.local/chalk/chalk.log;
  docker rm mem;
  docker run -it \
      --name mem \
      -v $PWD:$PWD \
      -w $PWD \
      -v (echo '
  exec.postexec.run = true
  exec.heartbeat = true
  ' | psub):/etc/chalk.c4m \
      -v $HOME/.local/chalk:/root/.local/chalk \
      -v ./chalk.json:/chalk.json \
      -v (echo '
  /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt
  ' | psub):/tmp/prep_postexec.txt \
      --entrypoint=$PWD/chalk \
      alpine \
      --trace exec --chalk-as-parent -- \
      /bin/sh -c '
  tail /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt
  sleep 20
  '
```

and then in another tab:

```
✗ while true; sleep 0.5;  docker container stats --no-stream --format '{{ .MemUsage }}' mem; end
```

author: gabrieldougherty
body:
This PR adds a comprehensive CI workflow using GitHub Actions that leverages our Nix flake for reproducible builds.

## Features:
- 🔄 **Reproducible builds** using the Nix flake configuration
- 🖥️ **Multi-platform support** (Ubuntu and macOS)
- ⚡ **GCC 14** compiler as configured in flake.nix
- 🧪 **Automated testing** by running all threading examples
- 📦 **Nix store caching** for faster builds
- 🔧 **Consistent environment** across local development and CI

## Workflow Details:
- Builds on both  and 
- Uses the same Nix flake environment as local development
- Runs all threading examples to verify functionality
- Includes caching to speed up subsequent builds

This ensures that our C++ threading project builds consistently across different platforms and maintains the same environment as our local Nix development setup.

Use a read loop and incoming channel so that we can select on incoming messages and unblock calls of ioConn.Read as soon as Close is called. This avoids the scenario of #224, where a close of the StdioTransport does not gracefully shut down the JSON-RPC connection.

Fixes #224

body:
## Summary

This PR implements a comprehensive dual-logger system with feature flag support, resolving persistent EventEmitter memory leak warnings and adding a CLI for managing experimental features.

## Major Changes

### 🔀 Dual-Logger Implementation
- Created abstraction layer supporting both Pino (default) and mcp-logger
- Added `mcpLoggerEnabled` feature flag with environment variable support
- Implemented factory pattern for logger selection based on feature flags
- Full backward compatibility maintained with existing logging API

### 🛡️ Memory Leak Prevention
- Implemented Pino instance caching by configuration hash
- Added child logger caching at multiple levels
- Fixed global logger management to prevent duplicate instances
- Shared transport instances to prevent exit listener accumulation
- Configurable process.setMaxListeners via `HYPERTOOL_MAX_LISTENERS` env var

### 🎛️ Feature Flag Management
- Added `hypertool-mcp config flags` CLI command
- Simple list/enable/disable operations for experimental features
- Support for `nedbEnabled` and `mcpLoggerEnabled` flags
- JSON-based persistence in config.json

### 🧪 Testing Improvements
- Separated performance tests using `.perf.test.ts` naming convention
- Added comprehensive logging integration tests
- Created memory leak specific test suite
- Fixed test environment to prevent warnings in parallel execution

## Technical Implementation

### Logger Architecture
- **Factory Pattern**: `logger/factory.ts` manages logger selection based on feature flags
- **Interfaces**: Common `LoggerInterface` ensures consistent API across implementations
- **Pino Implementation**: Direct Pino logger with proper transport management
- **MCP Logger Wrapper**: Wraps mcp-logger to match our interface requirements

### Memory Leak Solutions
1. **Instance Caching**: Pino instances are cached by configuration hash to prevent recreation
2. **Transport Reuse**: Shared transport instances prevent multiple exit listener registrations
3. **Child Logger Caching**: Both PinoLogger and Logger wrapper implement child caching
4. **Test Environment**: Increased max listeners for parallel test execution

### Feature Flag CLI
```bash
# List all feature flags
hypertool-mcp config flags list

# Enable mcp-logger
hypertool-mcp config flags enable mcpLoggerEnabled

# Disable a feature
hypertool-mcp config flags disable nedbEnabled
```

## Testing

- ✅ All existing tests pass
- ✅ New logging tests added (unit + integration)
- ✅ Memory leak tests specifically validate no warnings
- ✅ Performance tests separated to avoid false positives
- ✅ Feature flag CLI tested manually

## Breaking Changes

None - this PR maintains full backward compatibility.

## Environment Variables

New environment variables:
- `HYPERTOOL_MCP_LOGGER_ENABLED`: Enable mcp-logger (overrides config)
- `HYPERTOOL_MAX_LISTENERS`: Set process max listeners (default: 10)

## Review Notes

This PR resolves the persistent MaxListenersExceededWarning that was occurring even with the mcp-logger feature flag disabled. The root cause was Pino creating multiple instances with transports that register exit listeners. The solution implements proper instance caching and transport reuse.

The feature flag system allows us to gradually roll out experimental features like mcp-logger while maintaining stability with the default Pino implementation.

See [a talk](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aEntwyZL2RE&list=PL2KXbZ9-EY9QW4vewD7Lk6Mm6PJbWECOM&index=18) I gave about this ([slides](https://static.sched.com/hosted_files/spinnaker2022/1f/Managing%20Accounts%20Across%20AWS%20Partitions.pdf?_gl=1*2nspbg*_gcl_au*MTE4MjUxMDQ4MC4xNzU0MzU5MDg1*FPAU*MTE4MjUxMDQ4MC4xNzU0MzU5MDg1)).

There's a new configuration flag to enable this (defaults to false):
```
aws:
  loadAccounts:
    useManagingAccountProfile: true
```
If enabled, the new `managingAccountProfile` property of AWS accounts specifies the profile to use.

The tl;dr is that AWS doesn't support assuming a role across partitions.  So, before this PR, Spinnaker needed to run in the same partition as the accounts it targets.  With this PR, it's now possible for one Spinnaker instance to target multiple partitions.

body:
This PR implements a comprehensive visual dashboard for the flight delay prediction ML model to address the lack of visualization mentioned in the issue.

## Overview

The dashboard provides an interactive web interface that displays flight delay predictions with rich visual elements, allowing users to easily understand on-time vs delayed flight probabilities.

## Key Features

**Interactive Prediction Interface:**
- Dropdown selection for 70+ airports loaded from existing data
- Day-of-week selection (Monday through Sunday)
- Real-time ML predictions using the existing trained scikit-learn model

**Visual Elements:**
- Large percentage displays showing on-time and delay probabilities
- CSS-based donut chart visualization with color-coded segments (green for on-time, red for delayed)
- Interactive legend with exact percentages
- Live statistics tracking total predictions, average delay probability, and most queried airport

**Technical Implementation:**
- Self-contained Python HTTP server (`simple_server.py`) with no external dependencies
- Graceful fallback handling for model loading errors
- Responsive design that works on desktop and mobile
- RESTful API endpoints for predictions (`/predict`), airports (`/airports`), and statistics
- Comprehensive test suite covering model integration and dashboard functionality

## Usage

```bash
cd server
python simple_server.py
```

Access the dashboard at `http://localhost:8000`

## Example Prediction

For Tampa International Airport on Monday, the model predicts:
- **84.3% probability** of on-time arrival (displayed in green)
- **15.7% probability** of delay (displayed in red)

The visual chart makes it immediately clear which outcome is more likely, fulfilling the requirement to "show on-time flights and delay flights" with clear visual distinction.

## Testing

Added comprehensive test suite (`test_dashboard.py`) that validates:
- Model prediction accuracy and probability calculations
- Airport data loading and formatting
- Dashboard component functionality
- Parameter validation and error handling

All tests pass successfully, ensuring reliable operation.

## Screenshots

![Dashboard with Prediction Results](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e6edf36d-a04c-4f4a-93df-7fa14240dcd1)

The dashboard successfully transforms the raw ML predictions into an intuitive visual interface, making flight delay information accessible and actionable for users.

Fixes #1.

- Provides classes for quantum states, qubits, query plans, and a quantum query optimizer
- Supports asynchronous optimization and quantum metrics tracking
- Adds a query plan generator with quantum-inspired cost estimation

## Changes

### Core Quantum Optimization
- **QuantumState Enum**: Defines quantum states (superposition, entangled, collapsed)
- **Qubit Class**: Models quantum bits with measurement and reset functionality
- **QueryPlan Class**: Represents query execution plans with quantum state and probability
- **QuantumQueryOptimizer Class**: Implements quantum-inspired optimization algorithms including:
  - Superposition creation
  - Quantum interference to amplify good plans
  - Quantum annealing with tunneling to escape local minima
  - Asynchronous optimization support
  - Entanglement of query plans
  - Measurement to collapse superposition to final plan
  - Quantum metrics and state reset

- **QuantumQueryPlanGenerator Class**: Generates multiple query plans with varied join orders and filter placements

author: polarathene
body:
This PR addresses [feedback from another PR](https://github.com/EricLBuehler/candle-vllm/pull/238#discussion_r2252967000) I gave:
- APT: Use [DEB822 `.sources` format](https://repolib.readthedocs.io/en/latest/deb822-format.html) instead of deprecated `.list` format.
- Use Dockerfile HereDoc syntax.
- Use `-qq` ([implies `-y`](https://manpages.ubuntu.com/manpages/lunar/man8/apt-get.8.html)) for `apt-get` commands, and ensure consistent cleanup via `rm` is used in related `RUN` steps.

---

**NOTE:** I am not familiar with oneAPI or supporting it.

As this feature is not part of the official `mistral.rs` Dockerfile (_that it was [claimed to have been imported from](https://github.com/EricLBuehler/candle-vllm/pull/220)_), there is a `libomp-dev` runtime dependency (_since the original [`Dockerfile` contribution at `mistral.rs`](https://github.com/EricLBuehler/mistral.rs/pull/56)_), but not one associated to oneAPI as has been added into the `builder` stage (_presumably just for headers and symlink, at which point I wonder if the original runtime stage package had ever been required previously_ 🤷‍♂️).

Since the package has existed in the runtime stage from the beginning I've avoided shifting it into the MKL associated `RUN` or adding commentary, as I do not know if that is used by anything else?

---

## Regarding size of this dependency

Personally I am against monolithic images and mixing concerns from a maintenance and user perspectives. Mixing the MKL/oneAPI support with CUDA seems unnecessary and is definitely wasteful to users interested in building the image that aren't using either of these heavy dependencies.

Installing the `intel-oneapi-hpc-toolkit` package appears to add approx 12GB of weight, which in this case will be double due to it being additive to both build and runtime stages. It could possibly be optimized there but I don't have the hardware available to investigate.

CUDA is of similar weight for it's build image, but the runtime image is notably slimmer by comparison.

I presently lack a system with the disk space to build the full `Dockerfile`, but I assume it's rather large. The test `Dockerfile` I used spent the bulk of it's build time just installing the dep (_500 secs, about 80% of build time_), and that is with no builder stage involved.

---

I'd encourage separate image variants for such going forward.

The [existing support was snuck in](https://github.com/EricLBuehler/candle-vllm/pull/220) despite the contributor having already been advised for their related contribution at `mistral.rs` to [add `mkl` feature support as a separate image variant](https://github.com/EricLBuehler/mistral.rs/pull/1468#issuecomment-3042975846).

body:
## Issue

- resolve: route06/liam-internal#5244

## Why is this change needed?

The schema design tool was failing DDL validation when PostgreSQL schemas contained enum types referenced by tables. While the Drizzle parser could correctly parse enum definitions, the internal schema structure and DDL generation pipeline didn't support enums, causing "type does not exist" errors during validation.

## What changed?

### Core Schema Support
- **Extended Schema Definition**: Added `enums` field to the core Schema type with proper valibot validation
- **Enum DDL Generation**: Implemented PostgreSQL `CREATE TYPE ... AS ENUM` statement generation with proper escaping
- **DDL Ordering**: Ensured enums are created before tables that reference them in the DDL output

### Parser Integration  
- **Drizzle Converter**: Updated the Drizzle-to-internal schema converter to extract and include enum definitions
- **Type Safety**: Added enum support throughout the parsing pipeline while maintaining existing functionality

### Comprehensive Updates
- **TypeScript Fixes**: Updated 49 files across all packages to include the new `enums` property in schema objects
- **Test Coverage**: Added comprehensive tests for enum DDL generation, including edge cases and integration scenarios

## Key Technical Details

```mermaid
%%{ init : { "theme" : "default" }}%%
graph TD
    A[Drizzle Schema] --> B[Parse Enums]
    B --> C[Convert to Internal Schema]
    C --> D[Include Enums in Schema Object]
    D --> E[DDL Generation]
    E --> F[CREATE TYPE statements first]
    F --> G[CREATE TABLE statements]
    G --> H[Constraint statements]
```

The implementation ensures proper DDL ordering where enum types are created before any tables that reference them, preventing the "type does not exist" validation errors.

## Human Review Checklist

**Critical Items:**
- [ ] **DDL Ordering**: Verify that enum `CREATE TYPE` statements are generated before table definitions that use those enums
- [ ] **String Escaping**: Check that enum values with special characters are properly escaped in DDL generation
- [ ] **Parser Integration**: Validate that the Drizzle enum extraction correctly handles all enum definition patterns
- [ ] **Schema Migration**: Confirm that existing schemas without enums still work correctly with the new structure

**Testing & Type Safety:**
- [ ] **Test Coverage**: Review test cases for edge cases like empty enums, special characters, and complex enum usage
- [ ] **TypeScript Safety**: Verify that all schema object updates across packages maintain type consistency
- [ ] **Backward Compatibility**: Ensure that schemas without enums continue to function properly

## Implementation Notes

- The `anEnum` factory and related exports were intentionally kept internal to avoid unused export linting errors
- All existing schema objects required updates to include the `enums: {}` property for type compatibility
- DDL generation uses the existing PostgreSQL escaping utilities for consistency and security

author: ziris85
body:
## Description:
Hi there! This is mainly just a proposal for a quality-of-life adjustment stemming from my very-short-lived bug report #306 . Now that a client_id composed from the `discovery_device_name` is being passed along with the MQTT connection per #299 , this can cause connection conflict when more than one gateway is connecting to the same MQTT broker if one is lazy like myself and leaves the default configuration. So, this proposal is simply to change the default for that config and prepend the systems hostname to the configuration, making it by default `<hostname>-TheengsGateway`. This way, the name is less likely to cause conflict with multiple gateways!

An alternative idea I had was maybe to generate a short random string/UID to prepend instead of the hostname, but I thought the hostname might be more meaningful to ID the system it's running on.

Thoughts?

author: tonyd3
body:
**Multiple I/O uvloop threads for Coordinator** This pull request introduces a significant architectural change to the coordinator component by implementing a multi-threaded I/O model. Previously, the coordinator likely relied on a single I/O thread for all cluster communication. The core change involves abstracting the I/O runtime into `IORuntimeCtx` objects, each managing its own `libuv` event loop, request queue, and connection manager. The main `MRCluster` now maintains a pool of these `IORuntimeCtx` instances, distributing requests among them using a round-robin mechanism. The primary outcome of this change is enhanced scalability and performance for cluster operations by enabling parallel I/O. It aims to improve responsiveness and throughput, especially in high-concurrency scenarios. The refactoring also leads to better isolation of I/O operations and a more robust framework for handling dynamic topology updates and connection management across multiple threads.
Key Changes • Introduced ``IORuntimeCtx`` structure to encapsulate `libuv` event loop, request queue (``MRWorkQueue``), and connection manager (``MRConnManager``) for each I/O thread. • The ``MRCluster`` now manages a pool of ``IORuntimeCtx`` instances, distributing incoming requests (e.g., ``MR_Fanout``, ``MR_MapSingle``) across them using a round-robin strategy. • Refactored core cluster communication functions (``MRCluster_SendCommand``, ``MRCluster_FanoutCommand``, ``MRCluster_GetConn``) to operate on a specific ``IORuntimeCtx`` instance, rather than a single global connection manager. • Implemented thread-safe mechanisms for ``IORuntimeCtx`` creation, starting, and freeing, including synchronization primitives (``uv_mutex_t``, ``uv_cond_t``) to manage thread lifecycle. • Modified topology update logic (``MR_UpdateTopology``) to propagate new cluster topologies to all ``IORuntimeCtx`` instances, with each instance maintaining its own copy of the topology. • Updated connection pool resizing (``MR_UpdateConnPoolSize``) to dynamically adjust connections per ``IORuntimeCtx`` based on the new ```SEARCH_IO_THREADS``` configuration. • Added a new configuration option ```SEARCH_IO_THREADS``` to control the number of I/O threads used by the coordinator. • Enhanced shutdown procedures for ``IORuntimeCtx`` to ensure proper cleanup of `libuv` handles and graceful thread joining. • Refactored ```RQ``` (Request Queue) to be an integral part of ``IORuntimeCtx``, handling request pushing and popping in a thread-safe manner. • Introduced new C++ unit tests (``test_cpp_io_runtime_ctx`.cpp`, ``test_cpp_cluster_io_threads`.cpp`) to validate the behavior and thread safety of the new I/O runtime context and multi-threaded cluster operations. • Updated Python integration tests (``test_multithread`.py`, `test.py`, ``test_config`.py`) to account for the new multi-threaded I/O model and ```SEARCH_IO_THREADS``` configuration.
Affected Areas • src/coord/rmr/`io_runtime_ctx`.c • src/coord/rmr/`io_runtime_ctx`.h • src/coord/rmr/cluster.c • src/coord/rmr/cluster.h • src/coord/rmr/rmr.c • src/coord/rmr/rmr.h • src/coord/rmr/rq.c • src/coord/rmr/rq.h • src/coord/rmr/conn.c • src/coord/rmr/conn.h • src/coord/rmr/`cluster_topology`.c • src/coord/rmr/`cluster_topology`.h • src/coord/config.c • src/coord/config.h • src/module.c • src/coord/`debug_commands`.c • tests/pytests/`test_multithread`.py • tests/pytests/test.py • tests/pytests/`test_config`.py • tests/cpptests/`coord_tests`/`test_cpp_io_runtime_ctx`.cpp • tests/cpptests/`coord_tests`/`test_cpp_cluster_io_threads`.cpp • tests/cpptests/`coord_tests`/`CMakeLists`.txt • tests/ctests/`coord_tests`/`test_cluster`.c • tests/ctests/`coord_tests`/`CMakeLists`.txt • tests/cpptests/`CMakeLists`.txt • sbin/unit-tests

author: constellation
body:
#### a90e529da1cc5cc149294614ff6ca9fcd4568453 
[JSC] JS Lexer should not do double-lookup for dispatch
https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=296913
rdar://157533153

Reviewed by Keith Miller.

For dispatching, we do not need to lookup the type from
typesOfLatin1Characters. It turned out that this load is really hot, and
we should just directly dispatch the switch based on the coming
character.
The important thing is,

1. We should list up all 0 - 255 cases explicitly to make sure that
   LChar is dispatched somewhere. This leads to efficient code
   generation from the compiler.
2. We should not add the characters outside of 0 - 255 to keep the
   dispatch super efficient. That's why we reuse white space characters
   for non-latin1 identifier dispatching.

* Source/JavaScriptCore/parser/Lexer.cpp:
(JSC::Lexer<T>::lexWithoutClearingLineTerminator):

body:
# Description This PR is a merge of several upstream PRs. These consist of Einstein Engines No. 1536, 1560, 1563, 1574, 1585, 1650, 1663, 1667, 1711, and 1958. These PRs were cherry-picked using the -x option, and completed using CLI, retaining the cherry-picked commit info to the best of my ability. Below is a general summary of the PRs: - **1560** reworks Martial Artist to instead have a power attack as the base attack, while reducing the increases to unarmed damage and attack. This theoretically makes Martial Artist more attractive as it improves your chance to hit with unarmed attacks dramatically, while still dealing around the same DPS as before. This also gives the trait to the Boxer and Gladiator by default, and also the Martial Artist themselves if they haven't been already. Aplenty other melee adjustments, which can be seen in more detail in that PR. - **1563** makes it take longer to eat a brain, while also showing a big red popup indicating that someone might be round removed. Supposedly also includes a fix to make the flavor popup work for the recipient of a force-feeding. - **1574** finally makes handheld radios be tunable to different frequencies. This also includes the sec radio, it seems. - **1585, 1650, 1663, 1667, and 1711** is all together a refinement to the chemmaster's UI. A large improvement, in my opinion. - **1958** introduces the fill bot, which will gather things off the floor and put them into the lathe, silo, or dispos that they are linked to. - **1536** places the NTR, BSO, and the new Magistrate roles into their own department: CC Dignitaries. Note that this PR also included map changes for the Magistrate, which have been intentionally excluded from the cherry-pick. - Partial merge of **2136** to fix a erroneous test fail relating to an indestructible cyborg arm/hand, for some odd reason. --- # TODO - [x] Actually get images for the media section - [x] One final lookover ---

Media

--- # Changelog :cl: Einstein Engines - add: Handheld radios, including their security variant can now be tuned to specific frequencies, and have their mic and speaker toggled separately. - tweak: The Martial Artist trait has received a rework, and is now given for free to gladiators and boxers. - tweak: Eating a brain takes longer, along with a red popup to communicate potential round removal. - tweak: The Chemmaster's UI has been revised, and now features a pill buffer. - add: The fillbot has been added. Use a multi-tool or network analyzer to link it to a lathe, silo, or dispos and watch it pick everything up off the floor and into the linked object! - add: The Dignitary department, along with the Magistrate has been added. The BSO and NTR has been moved to this department.

author: yonyelm
body:
### 🚀 Deployment Infrastructure Integration

This PR introduces deployment support for the project using **Terraform**, **Docker Compose**, and **NGINX**, enabling full-stack deployment to AWS with PostgreSQL as the backend database.

### ✅ Summary of Changes

#### 🗂️ Deployment Folder

* Added `deployment/` directory containing:

  * `terraform.tf`: Automates infrastructure provisioning (VPC, EC2, RDS PostgreSQL, security groups, subnets, etc.).
  * `nginx.conf`: Configures NGINX to serve the React frontend and proxy API calls to the Spring Boot backend.
  * `docker-compose.yml`: Provides a local PostgreSQL setup for testing purposes.
  * `README.md`: Step-by-step deployment and teardown instructions using Terraform and Docker.

#### 🛠 Backend Configuration Updates

* **Profiles added**:

  * `application-dev.properties`
  * `application-gamma.properties`
  * `application-prod.properties`
* Updated default profile to `dev` via new `application.properties`.
* Backend now supports environment-specific configuration of:

  * **Database URLs and credentials**
  * **Image upload directories**

#### 🧠 Code Changes

* `StoreService` now uses `@Value` to inject `image.upload.dir` from properties files instead of hardcoded paths.
* Updated `.gitignore` to exclude Terraform-related files and sensitive `.tfvars`.

author: copilot
body:
This PR fixes the OpenGL renderer issue that was causing "Unable to match the desired swap behavior" errors, which were affecting UI performance and animations throughout the app.

## Root Cause
The issue was caused by three main problems:

1. **Missing hardware acceleration configuration** - The app didn't explicitly enable hardware acceleration in AndroidManifest.xml
2. **Conflicting window flags** - The BlackGlass theme used `FLAG_LAYOUT_NO_LIMITS` which interferes with OpenGL surface creation
3. **Incompatible theme settings** - Theme configurations weren't optimized for OpenGL rendering contexts

## Solution
The fix implements a comprehensive approach to ensure proper OpenGL compatibility:

### Core Changes
- **AndroidManifest.xml**: Added `android:hardwareAccelerated="true"` to enable hardware acceleration app-wide
- **BaseActivity.java**: Replaced problematic `FLAG_LAYOUT_NO_LIMITS` with safe status bar color configuration methods
- **styles.xml**: Added OpenGL compatibility settings (`windowIsTranslucent=false`, `windowDisablePreview=false`) to all themes

### New Utilities
- **OpenGLCompatibilityHelper**: A utility class that manages OpenGL configuration, clears problematic window flags, and provides safe system bar configuration
- **OpenGLRendererTest**: Comprehensive unit tests to verify the fixes work correctly
- **OpenGLTestActivity**: Manual testing activity for verification

### Enhanced Compatibility
The fix ensures proper OpenGL rendering across all app themes (Light, Dark, BlackGlass) while maintaining backward compatibility. The changes are minimal and targeted - only 39 lines modified in existing files, with the rest being new utilities and tests.

## Technical Details
Instead of using layout-affecting window flags that can cause OpenGL swap behavior issues, the solution uses:
- Direct `Window.setStatusBarColor()` and `Window.setNavigationBarColor()` calls
- `WindowInsetsControllerCompat` for status bar appearance
- Proper hardware acceleration at both application and window levels

The fix also includes debug utilities that log OpenGL configuration details when `BuildConfig.DEBUG` is enabled, making future troubleshooting easier.

Fixes #20.

author: zachbresler21
body:
## What
Fix infinite loop in embedding processing pipeline by adding message validation and improved error handling to prevent empty/invalid messages from being reprocessed indefinitely.

## Why
The embedding orchestrator was running every 5 minutes and claiming the same problematic messages repeatedly because:
- Messages with empty content were claimed but filtered out during processing, never marked as complete
- Batch failures in the worker caused all messages to remain unprocessed
- No distinction between retry-able and permanent failures
- Invalid messages would accumulate and consume processing capacity without progress

This resulted in the system processing the same 100 messages every 5 minutes instead of making progress through the queue.

## How
**Orchestrator Changes:**
- Added upfront message validation to filter empty/invalid content before sending to SQS
- Mark invalid messages as `needs_embedding = false` immediately 
- Added content length validation (max 100k characters)
- Improved logging for better debugging

**Worker Changes:**
- Process messages individually using `Promise.allSettled` instead of failing entire batches
- Added message validation with early filtering
- Classify errors as critical (mark as complete) vs retryable
- Mark messages with critical failures as not needing embedding
- Enhanced error handling for thread context building and embedding generation

**Infrastructure Updates:**
- Reduced SQS `maxReceiveCount` from 3 to 2 for faster failure detection
- Added long polling configuration for better efficiency

## Testing
- [ ] Tested locally with `npm run local:dev`

**Testing Details:**
- Test orchestrator with empty message content (should mark as not needing embedding)
- Test worker with invalid message data (should handle gracefully)
- Test batch processing with mixed valid/invalid messages
- Verify messages move through pipeline without getting stuck
- Monitor CloudWatch logs for proper error classification
- Test with messages exceeding 100k character limit

## Deployment Notes
- [x] SAM template updated (SQS configuration changes)
- [ ] Environment variables documented (no new variables added)
- [x] No breaking API changes

## Checklist
- [x] Code follows project style guidelines
- [x] Self-review completed
- [x] Complex code documented
- [ ] Related issues linked

## Related Issues
<!-- Link related issues using "Fixes #123" or "Closes #123" -->
Fixes infinite embedding processing loop causing high Lambda costs and preventing progress through message queue.

## Breaking Changes
None. Changes are backward compatible and improve existing functionality.

## Additional Notes
**Monitoring Recommendations:**
- Set up CloudWatch alarms for DLQ message count
- Monitor `needs_embedding = true` message count to ensure it decreases over time
- Track embedding processing success/failure rates

**Future Optimisations:**
- Consider adding retry count tracking to database schema
- Implement circuit breaker pattern for high failure rates
- Add health check to skip processing during system issues

**Key Metrics to Watch:**
- Messages stuck with `claimed_at` timestamp but `needs_embedding = true`
- DLQ message accumulation
- Embedding processing throughput vs input rate

body: ### Description This PR fixes a critical issue where `proto.Equal()` fails with "proto: don't know how to compare 0" error when comparing votes/proposals that only differ by timestamp. This bug prevents the timestamp reuse logic from working correctly, resulting in unnecessary "conflicting data" errors. ### Problem When multiple sentries request signatures for the same block with different timestamps, Horcrux should reuse the previous signature if the votes only differ by timestamp. However, `proto.Equal()` was failing to properly compare the protobuf messages, causing false negative comparisons and triggering "conflicting data" errors. The logs show: ``` All fields match (except timestamp) proto: don't know how to compare 0 [DEBUG] proto.Equal result: false Failed to sign type=prevote chain_id=injective-test-1 height=324792 round=0 error="conflicting data" ``` ### Root Cause The `proto.Equal()` function from gogoproto library encounters unknown fields or extensions in the protobuf messages unmarshalled via `protoio.UnmarshalDelimited()`. When it can't handle these fields, it logs "proto: don't know how to compare X" and returns false, even when all visible fields are identical. ### Solution Replace `proto.Equal()` with manual field-by-field comparison in both: - `checkVotesOnlyDifferByTimestamp()` - `checkProposalsOnlyDifferByTimestamp()` The manual comparison checks all relevant fields (Type, Height, Round, BlockID, ChainID) while ignoring any internal protobuf metadata that was causing the comparison to fail. ### Changes 1. **Manual field comparison**: Replaced `proto.Equal()` with explicit comparison of all fields 2. **Improved error handling**: Return false instead of panic on unmarshal errors 3. **Better nil handling**: Use XOR pattern `(a == nil) != (b == nil)` for clearer nil checks 4. **Added logging**: Log warnings when unmarshal fails for debugging ### Testing The fix has been verified to resolve the "conflicting data" errors in private testnet logs. The timestamp reuse logic now works correctly when votes/proposals only differ by timestamp. ### Impact This fix is critical for validators using multiple sentries, as it prevents unnecessary signing failures and reduces the risk of double signing by properly reusing signatures when appropriate.

author: beer-1
body:
# Description

This PR refines the emergency proposal activation process by introducing a manual activation mechanism and clarifying the activation rules. Previously, if a proposal was submitted by a whitelisted proposer, anyone could trigger its emergency status by depositing sufficient funds. Now, activation is restricted to:

- a final deposit made by a whitelisted account, or
- an explicit call to `MsgActivateEmergencyProposal` by a whitelisted caller.

### Activation Restrictions

✅ Only whitelisted addresses in `EmergencySubmitters` can activate
✅ Proposal must be in voting period
✅ Total deposit ≥ `EmergencyMinDeposit`
✅ Sender or depositor must be authorized emergency submitter

## Key Changes

### New Manual Activation Mechanism

- Added `MsgActivateEmergencyProposal`: New message type that allows authorized emergency submitters to manually activate emergency proposals
- Enhanced validation: Comprehensive checks for proposal status, deposit requirements, and sender authorization
- Improved error handling: Clear error messages for different failure scenarios

### Code Improvements
- Renamed message types: Simplified from `MsgAddEmergencyProposalSubmitters` to `MsgAddEmergencySubmitters` for consistency
- Fixed validation error message: Corrected "minimum deposit" to "expedited minimum deposit" in params validation
- Enhanced deposit logic: Improved emergency proposal activation during deposit processing
- Added comprehensive tests: New test cases for manual activation with various scenarios

name: Deploy a web application
  hosts: db_and_web_server
  vars:
    db_name: employee_db
    db_user: db_user
    db_password: Passw0rd
  tasks:
    - name: Install dependencies
      apt: name={{ item }} state=present
      with_items:
       - python
       - python-setuptools
       - python-dev
       - build-essential
       - python-pip
       - python-mysqldb

    - name: Install MySQL database
      apt:
        name: "{{ item }}"
        state:  present
      with_items:
       - mysql-server
       - mysql-client

    - name: Start Mysql Service
      service:
        name: mysql
        state: started
        enabled: yes

    - name: Create Application Database
      mysql_db: name={{ db_name }} state=present

    - name: Create Application DB User
      mysql_user: name={{ db_user }} password={{ db_password }} priv='*.*:ALL' host='%' state='present'

    - name: Install Python Flask dependencies
      pip:
        name: '{{ item }}'
        state: present
      with_items:
       - flask
       - flask-mysql

    - name: Copy web-server code
      copy: src=app.py dest=/opt/app.py

    - name: Start web-application
      shell: FLASK_APP=/opt/app.py nohup flask run --host=0.0.0.0 &

body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable-file -->

## Description
Changed the roles parameter on user_role to be able to take a list.
Also added a new parameter "remove_unlisted" which will default to false. This should mean the change is non-breaking for the moment, as the role list can also take a string, which will auto convert to list of one item.
In later versions (perhaps a major version?) The default should probably for remove_unlisted should probably change to true to make this module be more idempotent - but it may break compatibility with previously written tasks.

## How Has This Been Tested?
~~Manually tested locally - but needs testing against unit tests.~~
Have now added unit tests for new functionality, ~~but this also changed the output of module - breaking change maybe?~~
Added functionality now to give a compatibility mode where calling with using old parameters gives old style output. Using new "roles" parameter gives new output including diff.

body:
This PR updates the decorator from @torch.no_grad() to @torch.inference_mode() in the Qwen3-Reranker implementation.

torch.inference_mode() is a more optimized context for inference-only workloads, as it disables autograd and activates additional internal optimizations to reduce CPU overhead and improve execution speed. This change should not affect numerical results but can lead to better runtime performance and lower memory usage during inference.

import asyncio, runpy
q = runpy.run_path('bot/queue.py')
number_queue = q['number_queue']
user_queue = q['user_queue']
number_queue_lock = q['number_queue_lock']
user_queue_lock = q['user_queue_lock']

async def task1():
    async with number_queue_lock:
        number_queue.append(1)
        await asyncio.sleep(0.05)
        number_queue.popleft()

async def task2():
    async with user_queue_lock:
        user_queue.append(1)
        await asyncio.sleep(0.05)
        user_queue.popleft()

async def main():
    await asyncio.gather(task1(), task2())
    print('done', len(number_queue), len(user_queue))

asyncio.run(main())

author: olympichek
body:
This PR is an attempt to implement proof generation using existing code for computations on the GPU.

Precisely, this PR contains the following changes:
- I added the `expandBits` function to `JsonBuilder` - the inverse of `compactBits`
- functions used for common operations on the GPU (e.g. `squareInPlace` and `mulInPlace*`) are moved from `App` to `NttEngine` to allow reuse of them in `ProofSet`
- `squareInPlace` function had some code commented out and didn't work as is. I updated this function - now it's implementation is similar to `mulInPlace5`
- I added the `powInPlace` function. It's implementation is similar to `mersennePowMod` used previously, but it uses  `squareInPlace` and `mulInPlace5` to perform computation on the GPU
- `ProofSet::computeProof` is updated to use these GPU operations instead of GMP

The proof generation time on RTX 3090 for M3021377 is just 3 seconds now. The proof is successfully verified with PRPLL.
This PR can benefit from thorough code review and more extensive testing though.

body:
This PR adds detailed technical documentation explaining how ClashX implements system proxy configuration on macOS. The documentation was created in response to a user inquiry about the specific code locations and core technical logic behind the system proxy functionality.

## What's Added

Four comprehensive documentation files in Chinese:

1. **ClashX_系统代理实现分析.md** - Complete technical analysis covering:
   - Overall architecture using privileged helper daemon pattern
   - Core components (ProxyConfigHelper, SystemProxyManager, PrivilegedHelperManager)
   - Security mechanisms and permission management
   - Detailed code flow explanations

2. **ClashX_技术流程图.md** - Visual diagrams and flowcharts showing:
   - System architecture with XPC communication
   - Step-by-step proxy enabling/disabling workflows
   - Helper daemon installation process
   - Network interface configuration hierarchy

3. **ClashX_代码示例.md** - Code examples demonstrating:
   - Complete call chain from user interaction to system configuration
   - XPC service implementation in the helper daemon
   - SystemConfiguration framework usage
   - Authorization Services integration

4. **回答用户问题.md** - Direct answers to user questions about:
   - Exact file locations of core proxy code
   - Technical implementation details
   - Core technologies and frameworks used

## Key Technical Insights Documented

The analysis reveals ClashX uses a sophisticated **privilege separation architecture**:

```
User App (ClashX.app) ←→ XPC Communication ←→ Privileged Helper (ProxyConfigHelper)
   No system permissions                          Administrator privileges
```

**Core Implementation**:
- Uses macOS **SystemConfiguration.framework** to modify network proxy settings
- **Authorization Services** for privilege management
- **XPC (Cross-Process Communication)** for secure inter-process communication
- **SMJobBless** for privileged helper daemon installation

**Security Features**:
- Main app runs without system privileges
- Helper daemon isolated with minimal required permissions
- Code signing verification during installation
- Standard Apple frameworks for system integration

This documentation serves as a comprehensive reference for developers wanting to understand ClashX's proxy implementation or implement similar functionality in their own applications.

本 PR 包含两个主要更新：

2. **数据库用户管理**：添加了README.md和数据库用户命名规范

- ✅ 消除复杂的嵌套循环和条件语句

- ✅ 提高代码的可测试性和可重用性

- `data_processor.py` - 原始命令式版本（作为对比基准）
- `data_processor_functional.py` - 重构后的函数式版本
- `test_functional_processor.py` - 完整的测试套件
- `CODE_REVIEW_REPORT.md` - 详细的代码审查报告

### 数据库管理文件
- `README.md` - 项目介绍和数据库用户命名规范

## 🚀 函数式编程主要改进

### 1. 纯函数设计
- 将所有业务逻辑拆分为纯函数
- 消除副作用，提高可预测性
- 易于单元测试和调试

```python
# 重构前：复杂的嵌套逻辑
def process_data_files(self, file_paths):
    for file_path in file_paths:
        if not os.path.exists(file_path):
            # 错误处理
        else:
            # 深度嵌套的处理逻辑...

# 重构后：函数式管道
def process_data_files(self, file_paths):
    all_records = list(chain.from_iterable(
        map(self.file_processor, file_paths)
    ))
    processed_records = list(filter(
        lambda x: x is not None,
        map(self.record_processor, all_records)
    ))
    return sort_by_id(remove_duplicates_by_id(processed_records))
```

### 2. 高阶函数应用
- 使用高阶函数创建可配置的处理管道
- 提高代码的灵活性和可重用性

```python
def create_validator(required_fields, type_validators):
    def validate_record(record):
        # 验证逻辑
    return validate_record

def create_transformer(field_transformers):
    def transform_record(record):
        # 转换逻辑
    return transform_record
```

### 3. 函数组合
- 使用函数组合构建复杂的处理管道
- 提高代码的模块化程度

```python
def compose(*functions):
    return reduce(lambda f, g: lambda x: f(g(x)), functions, lambda x: x)

process_pipeline = compose(
    sort_by_id,
    remove_duplicates_by_id,
    partial(filter, lambda x: x is not None)
)
```

### 4. 不可变数据结构
- 避免修改原始数据
- 提高线程安全性和调试友好性

| 指标 | 原始代码 | 重构后代码 | 改进幅度 |
|------|----------|------------|----------|
| 圈复杂度 | 高 (>15) | 低 (<5) | ↓ 70% |
| 方法长度 | 100+ 行 | <30 行 | ↓ 70% |
| 重复代码 | 多处重复 | 无重复 | ↓ 90% |
| 测试覆盖率 | 困难测试 | 易于测试 | ↑ 80% |

### 改进点
1. **可读性**: 代码结构更清晰，逻辑更容易理解
2. **可维护性**: 模块化设计使得修改和扩展更加容易

body:
Older versions stored the tracktrace numbers not as array but as single value. When retrieved from the db a numeric tracktrace number would be converted to a float by json_decode, this would trip up the explode function further down which expects a string.
By instructing json_decode to return large ints as string, this is mitigated.

INT-1109

body:
#### 4f0c0eb24e9b1b2d4d6e69d6f2b6b60a8420a0e8 
[Form Control Refresh] `accent-color` should preserve control legibility
https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=244233
rdar://99018889

Reviewed by Aditya Keerthi.

When form control refresh is enabled, controls with tint color now preserve
legibility regardless of any set `accent-color`. To ensure that all controls can display
the same accent-colors, while also taking into account the fact that some controls
may not be able to use certain accent-colors without extensive changes to other parts
of the contol, the visual accent-color is bounded based on whether light mode or dark
mode is being used. In light mode, accent-colors with a luminance greater than 0.5
will have their luminance lowered to 0.5. In dark mode, accent-colors with a luminance
less than or equal to 0.5 will have their luminance increased to 0.5. For both
operations, the color's hue is preserved.

Additionally, checkboxes and radio buttons will now use a dark indicator in
cases where the accent-color luminance is greater than 0.5.

The threshold of 0.5 luminance was chosen to match AppKit's threshold for switching
indicator colors for checkboxes and radio buttons.

`setInsideDisabledSubmitButton` is now `setInsideSubmitButton` and is applied to
all submit buttons, regardless of enabled/disabled state in order to properly set
the text color based on enablement, the window active state, and the controls tint
color in order to preserve contrast.

Affected controls:
* <input type=range> (sliders)
* <input type=checkbox>
* <input type=radio>
* <input type=text list=somedatalist> (list buttons)
* <input type="submit">
* <progress>

body:
## 概要
CloudFront URLアクセス時に常に404ページが表示される問題の根本原因を修正しました。

## 問題
- https://dz2a9qu3y643s.cloudfront.net にアクセスすると必ず`/NotFound`にリダイレクトされる
- PR #70の修正後も問題が解決しなかった

## 原因
`getStateFromPath`関数のロジックに問題があり、正常なルートでも`NotFound`を返していました：
```typescript
// 削除した問題のあるコード
if (\!state || state.routes.length === 0) {
  return {
    routes: [{ name: 'NotFound' }],
  };
}
```

## 修正内容
- 不要な`getStateFromPath`関数を削除
- React Navigationのデフォルトのルーティング動作に任せる

## テスト手順
1. デプロイ完了後、https://dz2a9qu3y643s.cloudfront.net にアクセス
2. トップページが正しく表示されることを確認（/NotFoundにリダイレクトされない）
3. 各ページでリロードしても正常に動作することを確認

## 関連PR
- #69: CloudFront SPA 404エラー修正（インフラ側）
- #70: CloudFront URLをprefixesに追加

author: srlch
body:
This is the subsequent update based on this PR #58055

## Why I'm doing:

Disaster recovery based on cluster snapshot is implemented in StarRocks shared-data mode. The data in a cluster snapshot may be newer than the metadata version, potentially containing additional data files written after the metadata version. When a cluster is restored from a cluster snapshot, it needs to align the data with the metadata. To speed up the recovery process, only necessary data alignment is performed during the restoration. After the cluster is restored, some useless data might be left on the object storage. These useless data do not affect the normal operation of the cluster but occupy storage space unnecessarily, leading to storage waste. Full vacuum is used to delete these useless data to reclaim storage space.

## What I'm doing:

FullVacuum RPC implementation on backend
1. Before the orphaned data file cleanup starts, VacuumFull will delete metadata files which satisfy the following: (meta commit time < grace timestamp AND not in retain version list AND min_check_version <= ver < max_check_version)
2. Then, orphaned data files will be determined. We use min_active_txn_id to filter out new data files, then we open any remaining metadata files and note that the data files referenced are not orphans.

New Daemon on the frontend which triggers full vacuum on each partition every 24 hours (configurable)
1. Basically a copy of the AutoVacuumDaemon, except it triggers a different RPC and has different frequency
2. Unlike AutoVacuum, we don't broadcast requests based on tablet owners, since each RPC is handled by just a single CN (it's doing work for an entire partition, not just a set of tablets). Because it's not obvious to which CN a given request should be sent, this just choose a CN by random.

Fixes #issue

author: jcrpaquin
body:
# What?

This enables any field to be used with the bitset query parser via the CSV format parser. Any values passed in will be looked up, one at a time, to locate the first doc matching each.
> [!WARNING]
> Searching for non-unique values will produce non-exhaustive bitsets.

# Why?

Not all records have bibcodes and we'd like the flexibility to use other identifiers. In particular, we're moving towards using [SciX IDs, an internal ID representation](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1fKua6x-by0vfpu6yarUm1f0Z2QD2YVKTtpNbVbD7gAw), for all of our infrastructure.

author: wolegechu
body:
Per [RFC 0001](https://github.com/StepCastAI/stepcast-store/blob/main/rfcs/0001-distributed-virtual-memory-pool.md) §4.3, CPU memory release after GPU copy is now mandatory.

This change:
1. Removes the auto_release_cpu_after_gpu_copy flag from all structs
2. Updates MemoryManager to always release CPU memory after GPU copy
3. Integrates DVMP lock/unlock/evict calls for proper chunk management
4. Updates tests to remove the disabled auto-release code path
5. Updates documentation to reflect the mandatory behavior

The new flow:
- Before copy: lock_chunks() to mark chunks as LOCKED_TX
- After successful copy: unlock_chunks(copied_gpu=true) + evict_tail_bytes()
- Release CPU resources and transition state to UNALLOCATED

This prevents memory bloat and ensures consistent behavior across all model loading scenarios.

Closes #4

## Descriptions

This PR refactors the reward distribution system from block-height based to timestamp-based calculations across multiple modules including emission, staker, launchpad, and governance.

### Key Changes:

- Emission & GNS Module: Refactored distribution logic to use timestamps instead of block heights for more accurate time-based reward calculations
- Gov/Staker Module: Updated reward managers (emission and protocol fee) to calculate rewards based on elapsed time rather than block intervals
- Launchpad Module: Converted project durations and reward calculations from block-based to timestamp-based logic
- Governance Module: Adjusted execution methods and parameter registry to support timestamp-based operations

### Technical Details:

- Removed block height dependencies in favor of std.GetTimestamp() for time calculations
- Updated reward state tracking to use timestamps for last update times
- Modified halving logic to work with timestamp-based periods
- Simplified distribution calculations by using direct time differences

### Test Plan

- All existing unit tests pass with updated timestamp logic
- Scenario tests validate correct reward distribution over time
- Governance execution tests confirm proper timestamp-based operations
- Launchpad tier duration tests verify timestamp-based project lifecycles
- Integration tests confirm cross-module compatibility
- Manual testing of reward claiming and distribution flows

author: eshaham
body:
## Summary

This PR refactors the recipe structure to unify ecosystem-specific and ecosystem-agnostic recipes into a single, more maintainable structure with mandatory base `fix.md` files and optional variant-specific additions.

## Key Changes

### 🏗️ **Unified Recipe Structure**
- **All recipes** now require a mandatory `fix.md` file with base instructions
- **Optional `variants/` directory** for ecosystem-specific additions
- **Content concatenation**: `baseContent + '\n\n' + variantContent`
- **Removed old `fixes/` directory** structure (clean break)

### 🔧 **Core Implementation**
- **Type Definitions**: Added `getBaseFixContent()`, `getVariantContent()`, `getFixContentForVariant()` methods
- **Recipe Loading**: Modified `parseFixFiles()` to require `fix.md` and support `variants/` directory
- **Enhanced Validation**: Immediate failure when `fix.md` is missing, warnings for missing variants
- **Template Updates**: Fixed metadata template and enhanced magic generation templates

### 🤖 **Magic Generation Improvements**
- **Intelligent Level Selection**: Claude Code SDK now determines appropriate recipe levels (`workspace-only`, `project-only`, `workspace-preferred`)
- **Enhanced Templates**: Comprehensive level selection guidelines for AI generation
- **Conditional Template Variables**: Level field excluded during magic generation, allowing AI to choose

### 🧪 **Testing & Quality**
- **All 126 tests updated** to work with new structure
- **Fixed React component** state update timing issues in CLI
- **Comprehensive mock data** updates for new file structure
- **Pre-commit hooks passing** with linting and type checking

### 📚 **Documentation**
- **Updated README.md and docs/recipes.md** to reflect new unified structure
- **Added content concatenation examples** and variant usage patterns
- **Fixed all references** from `fixes/` to `variants/` directory

## Migration Impact

This change provides the foundation for future recipe migration and enhanced validation features.

## Testing

```bash
# Verify all tests pass
npm test

# Test recipe generation
npx chorenzo recipes generate test-recipe --category test --summary "Test recipe"

# Test recipe validation
npx chorenzo recipes validate test-recipe
```

## Before/After Structure

**Before** (ecosystem-specific):
```
recipe/
├── metadata.yaml
├── prompt.md
└── fixes/
    ├── javascript_eslint.md
    └── python_ruff.md
```

**After** (unified):
```
recipe/
├── metadata.yaml
├── prompt.md
├── fix.md              # Base instructions
└── variants/           # Optional additions
    ├── javascript_eslint.md
    └── python_ruff.md
```

author: copilot
body:
This PR upgrades the project from the deprecated `aws-sdk-go` v1 to the modern `aws-sdk-go-v2`. The AWS SDK for Go v1 has been deprecated and AWS recommends migrating to v2 for better performance, security, and ongoing support.

## Changes Made

### Core Changes
- **Updated imports**: Replaced `github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go/aws/session` with `github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/config`
- **Modernized AWS configuration**: Replaced `session.NewSession()` with `config.LoadDefaultConfig(context.Background())`
- **Updated credential retrieval**: Changed from `sess.Config.Credentials.GetWithContext(ctx)` to `cfg.Credentials.Retrieve(ctx)`

### Dependencies
- **Removed**: `github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go v1.55.7` (deprecated)
- **Added**: `github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/config v1.27.27` (modern replacement)
- All other AWS SDK v2 dependencies were already present as indirect dependencies

### Documentation
- Updated AWS SDK documentation link from v1 session docs to v2 config docs

### Testing
- Added unit tests to verify AWS MSK IAM SASL configuration works correctly
- All existing tests continue to pass
- Project builds successfully without any breaking changes

## Functionality Preserved

The AWS MSK IAM authentication functionality remains exactly the same from a user perspective:
- Same configuration format (`sasl.method=awsmskiam`)
- Same AWS credential sourcing behavior
- Same environment variables and AWS profile support
- Same error handling patterns

## Benefits

- **Security**: AWS SDK v2 includes latest security improvements
- **Performance**: Better memory usage and faster credential resolution
- **Maintenance**: Ongoing support and updates from AWS
- **Future-proofing**: Ensures compatibility with future AWS services and features

The upgrade is backward compatible and requires no changes to existing configurations or usage patterns.

body:
Besides the optimization, it also fixes this issue:
```
java.lang.IllegalStateException: Cannot decode [json.akka.io/akka.Done$] message type. Class mapping not found.
	at akka.javasdk.impl.serialization.JsonSerializer.fromBytes(JsonSerializer.scala:215)
	at akka.javasdk.impl.workflow.ReflectiveWorkflowRouter.decodeInput(ReflectiveWorkflowRouter.scala:73)
	at akka.javasdk.impl.workflow.ReflectiveWorkflowRouter.applyTransitionFunc$1(ReflectiveWorkflowRouter.scala:194)
	at akka.javasdk.impl.workflow.ReflectiveWorkflowRouter.getNextStep(ReflectiveWorkflowRouter.scala:204)
	at akka.javasdk.impl.workflow.WorkflowImpl.liftedTree1$1(WorkflowImpl.scala:301)
	at akka.javasdk.impl.workflow.WorkflowImpl.transition(WorkflowImpl.scala:299)
	at kalix.runtime.EmbeddedSdkDispatch$$anon$4.$anonfun$transition$1(EmbeddedSdkDispatch.scala:147)
	at scala.concurrent.Future$.$anonfun$apply$1(Future.scala:687)
```

it's because we register a mapping for `json.akka.io/akka.Done` (without $), we could extend the `reversedTypeHints` with additional mapping, but we don't need all the complex deserialization logic for `Done`, we can return the payload immediately.

author: joze-liburn
body:
We introduce a command line structure. The idea is to have

```
uibakery serve ...
```

command to start the web service; and then to have additional commands to allow maintenance operations. At the first iteration, there are two commands, operating upon the database-based message queue, implemented in this PR:

```
uibakery queue claim
```

Claims some free messages and prints the claim-id (and number of messages claimed).

```
uibakery queue unclaim --claim-id
```

Unclaims all the messages with a given claim id.

```
uibakery queue count
```

Counts queue messages by submission status, destination, and claim status.

```
uibakery queue list-claims [--status]
```

Lists all claims in the database queue. If a status is given, then lists and counts only the claims in that status.

---

- [spf13/cobra](https://github.com/spf13/cobra/) library is used to process command line arguments. This library dictates the command structure.
- [spf13/viper](https://github.com/spf13/viper) library is used, in conjunction with cobra, to allow (selected) parameters to be passed over using environment variables, configuration files and such.

body:
Updates the changelog formatting for LTS releases to use a simplified format without the c10s version prefix, addressing reviewer feedback.

**Problem:**
- Previous format: `LTS (c10s.20250309)`
- Required format: `LTS 20250309`

**Root Cause:**
The changelog generator was applying the same formatting logic to LTS releases as other release types, including the c10s version prefix and parentheses.

**Solution:**
Modified `.github/changelogs.py` to handle LTS releases with a surgical override approach:

- Preserves original formatting logic completely unchanged for all non-LTS release types
- Adds LTS-specific override that replaces the formatted result after original processing
- LTS releases now use format: `LTS YYYYMMDD` (no parentheses, no c10s prefix)
- Non-LTS releases maintain exact original format and behavior
- Maintains backward compatibility for all other release types

**Implementation:**
The fix uses an override approach where the original formatting logic runs unchanged, and then LTS releases have their result replaced with the simplified format. This ensures zero impact on existing functionality while achieving the required LTS format.

Fixes #384.

body:
This pull request (PR) is a follow-up to the previous PR [#31987](https://github.com/trustwallet/assets/pull/31987). 

deleting the old token's logo to avoid user's confusion 



### Issue Overview

Two "**BRG**" Tokens:
The deprecated "**Bridge Token**"
The new "**Bridge AI**" token


User Confusion: In the "**Swap**" tab of the application, there is no clear distinction between these two tokens, making it difficult for users to identify which token they are interacting with.

### Impact
The lack of differentiation between the deprecated "**Bridge Token**" and the new "**Bridge AI**" token in the "**Swap**" tab increases the risk of users inadvertently using the deprecated token. This has resulted in financial losses and negatively affects the user experience.

Proposed Solution
removing the old "Bridge Token"'s logo to ensure user's wont use it while doing the swap.

### Screenshots of the Problem

Screenshots demonstrating the issue are available in the PR comments for reference:
[Screenshot 1](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3c91b834-ff35-4426-b5a7-dde23a8c3730): Shows the two "BRG" tokens listed without clear differentiation.
![IMG_5236](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3c91b834-ff35-4426-b5a7-dde23a8c3730)

The BRG contract migration was carried out in three public stages, each officially announced on our verified X (Twitter) account:

author: copilot
body:
This PR implements a comprehensive update to the app configuration system and platform selection interface, addressing the requirements for better platform management and improved user experience.

## 🔄 Configuration Structure Changes

The app configuration structure has been modernized from the old format:
```json
{
    "ios": [/* iOS app configurations */],
    "android": [/* Android app configurations */],
    "pc": [/* Desktop app configurations */]
}
```

To a new, more flexible structure:
```json
{
    "config": {
        "additionalLocales": ["fa", "ru", "zh"]
    },
    "platforms": {
        "ios": [/* iOS app configurations */],
        "android": [/* Android app configurations */],
        "linux": [/* linux Desktop app configurations */],
        "macos": [/* macos Desktop app configurations */],
        "windows": [/* windows Desktop app configurations */],
        "androidTV": [/* androidTV app configurations */],
        "appleTV": [/* appleTV app configurations */]
    }
}
```

## 🎨 UI/UX Improvements

### Before: Long Platform Tabs
The old interface used horizontal tabs that could become unwieldy with many platforms.

### After: Clean Platform Selector
![Platform Selector](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/64bb055d-bc57-46d4-a37e-4bc89ed88979)

The new interface features:
- **"Доступные приложения" (Available Apps)** title on the left
- **Platform selector button** on the right showing current OS with icon and dropdown arrow
- **Modal selection interface** when clicked

![Platform Modal](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cd35ee7e-efd3-4f8b-903a-6ce9333f531a)

## ✨ Key Features

### Dynamic Platform Display
- Only displays platforms that have available applications
- Eliminates "No apps available for this platform" errors
- Smart filtering based on actual content

### Enhanced Platform Support
Expanded from 3 to 7 supported platforms:
- 🤖 **Android** - Android robot icon
- 🍎 **iOS** - Apple logo icon  
- 🪟 **Windows** - Windows logo icon
- 🍎 **macOS** - Apple logo icon (same as iOS)
- 🖥️ **Linux** - Monitor icon
- 📺 **Android TV** - TV icon
- 📺 **Apple TV** - TV icon

### Smart Platform Detection
The system automatically selects the most appropriate platform based on user agent:
- iOS devices → iOS platform
- Android devices → Android platform (or Android TV if detected)
- Desktop users → Windows/macOS/Linux based on OS detection

### Responsive Design
- Mobile-optimized modal interface
- Proper touch targets and spacing
- Material Design 3 styling throughout

## 🔧 Technical Implementation

### Backward Compatibility
- Automatically converts old config format to new structure
- Legacy 'pc' platform maps to 'windows'
- Existing applications continue to work without changes

### Translation Support
Added proper internationalization:
- Russian: "Выберите платформу"
- English: "Select Platform"

### New Functions
- `getPlatformIcon(platform)` - SVG icon management
- `createPlatformSelectModal()` - Modal interface
- `hasAnyApps(apps)` - Dynamic platform filtering
- Enhanced `setupOSTabs()` - New UI implementation

## 📱 Mobile Responsive
The interface is fully responsive with:
- Optimized modal sizing for mobile devices
- Proper padding and spacing adjustments
- Touch-friendly interaction areas
- Consistent Material Design 3 theming

This update significantly improves the user experience while maintaining full backward compatibility with existing configurations.

body:
This PR adds a new GitHub Actions workflow that enables automated rebasing and merging of pull requests based on labels or PR body content.

## What this workflow does

The new `.github/workflows/auto-rebase-merge.yml` workflow provides:

- **Smart triggering**: Activates on PR events (opened, synchronize, reopened, labeled) and supports manual dispatch
- **Label-based automation**: Automatically processes PRs with the `auto-merge` label or `[auto-merge]` in the PR body
- **Draft/WIP protection**: Skips processing for draft PRs or those marked with `[WIP]` in the title
- **Automatic rebasing**: Rebases PR branches against the target branch to resolve conflicts
- **Squash merging**: Uses squash merge strategy with standardized commit messages
- **Bot approval**: Auto-approves PRs created by GitHub Actions bot
- **Slack notifications**: Sends success/failure notifications via webhook

## Key features

1. **Conditional execution**: Only runs when specific conditions are met (labels or body text)
2. **Conflict resolution**: Automatically attempts to rebase branches to resolve merge conflicts
3. **Force push capability**: Updates PR branches with rebased commits
4. **Notification system**: Integrates with Slack for team awareness
5. **Manual override**: Can be triggered manually via workflow dispatch

This workflow complements the existing `auto-rebase-and-merge.yml` workflow but provides more comprehensive automation with better filtering and notification capabilities.

## Usage

To use this workflow:
1. Add the `auto-merge` label to a PR, or
2. Include `[auto-merge]` in the PR description, or
3. Manually trigger via Actions tab

The workflow will handle the rest automatically, ensuring PRs are properly rebased and merged with appropriate notifications.

author: zorinanton
body:
This PR introduces support for dynamic scalar User-Defined Functions (UDFs) for round-trip conversion between Substrait plans and Calcite RelNodes.

It establishes the Substrait YAML extension files as the single source of truth (SSoT) for all function signatures. The primary addition is a new utility, [YamlToSqlOperator](https://github.com/ZorinAnton/substrait-java/blob/ad11957f3c02f1383dc5128fad83763431422341/isthmus/src/main/java/io/substrait/isthmus/YamlToSqlOperator.java#L25), which acts as a bridge between the Substrait and Calcite worlds by dynamically generating Calcite SqlOperator objects from the parsed YAML definitions.

The implementation is optimized to only generate these operators for functions that are truly dynamic —that is, functions present in the provided extensions but not already defined in the default [SubstraitOperatorTable](https://github.com/ZorinAnton/substrait-java/blob/ad11957f3c02f1383dc5128fad83763431422341/isthmus/src/main/java/io/substrait/isthmus/calcite/SubstraitOperatorTable.java#L26).

Key Changes:
- New [YamlToSqlOperator](https://github.com/ZorinAnton/substrait-java/blob/ad11957f3c02f1383dc5128fad83763431422341/isthmus/src/main/java/io/substrait/isthmus/YamlToSqlOperator.java#L25) Utility: A type-safe converter that translates [SimpleExtension.ExtensionCollection](https://github.com/ZorinAnton/substrait-java/blob/ad11957f3c02f1383dc5128fad83763431422341/core/src/main/java/io/substrait/extension/SimpleExtension.java#L569) objects into a List<SqlOperator>. 

- Enhanced SqlToSubstrait (SQL → Substrait): The [SqlToSubstrait ](https://github.com/ZorinAnton/substrait-java/blob/ad11957f3c02f1383dc5128fad83763431422341/isthmus/src/main/java/io/substrait/isthmus/SqlToSubstrait.java#L40) constructor is updated to:

  - Identify dynamic UDFs by filtering the loaded extensions against the known operators in [SubstraitOperatorTable](https://github.com/ZorinAnton/substrait-java/blob/ad11957f3c02f1383dc5128fad83763431422341/isthmus/src/main/java/io/substrait/isthmus/calcite/SubstraitOperatorTable.java#L26).

  - Use [YamlToSqlOperator](https://github.com/ZorinAnton/substrait-java/blob/ad11957f3c02f1383dc5128fad83763431422341/isthmus/src/main/java/io/substrait/isthmus/YamlToSqlOperator.java#L25) to generate operators for these dynamic UDFs.

  - Inject the new operators into [Calcite's validator](https://github.com/ZorinAnton/substrait-java/blob/ad11957f3c02f1383dc5128fad83763431422341/isthmus/src/main/java/io/substrait/isthmus/SqlToSubstrait.java#L48) via a сhained SqlOperatorTable.

- Enhanced [SubstraitToCalcite ](https://github.com/ZorinAnton/substrait-java/blob/ad11957f3c02f1383dc5128fad83763431422341/isthmus/src/main/java/io/substrait/isthmus/SubstraitToCalcite.java#L96) (Substrait → SQL): The [SubstraitRelNodeConverter ](https://github.com/ZorinAnton/substrait-java/blob/ad11957f3c02f1383dc5128fad83763431422341/isthmus/src/main/java/io/substrait/isthmus/SubstraitRelNodeConverter.java#L141)is similarly enhanced to:

  - Also identify dynamic UDFs from the provided [SimpleExtension.ExtensionCollection](https://github.com/ZorinAnton/substrait-java/blob/ad11957f3c02f1383dc5128fad83763431422341/core/src/main/java/io/substrait/extension/SimpleExtension.java#L569).

  - Dynamically create [FunctionMappings.Sig](https://github.com/ZorinAnton/substrait-java/blob/ad11957f3c02f1383dc5128fad83763431422341/isthmus/src/main/java/io/substrait/isthmus/expression/FunctionMappings.java#L125) objects for these UDFs, enabling the [ScalarFunctionConverter ](https://github.com/ZorinAnton/substrait-java/blob/ad11957f3c02f1383dc5128fad83763431422341/isthmus/src/main/java/io/substrait/isthmus/expression/ScalarFunctionConverter.java#L21) to correctly map them back to their SqlOperator during plan conversion.

- Architectural Refactoring: The EXTENSION_COLLECTION in [SqlConverterBase ](https://github.com/ZorinAnton/substrait-java/blob/ad11957f3c02f1383dc5128fad83763431422341/isthmus/src/main/java/io/substrait/isthmus/SqlConverterBase.java#L22) has been changed from static final to an instance field to allow for the dynamic configuration required by this feature.

author: copilot
body:
The infomap community detection was failing with `FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'out/tmpedgelist.tree'` because the required output directory wasn't being created before running the infomap binary.

## Problem

When calling `infomap_communities()`, the function would:
1. Create an edgelist file (e.g., `./tmp/tmpedgelist.txt`)
2. Call the infomap binary with `"out/"` as the output directory
3. Try to parse the results from `"out/tmpedgelist.tree"`

However, if the `out/` directory didn't exist, the infomap binary would fail silently with exit code 1, leaving no output file to parse.

## Solution

Added directory creation in two strategic locations:

```python
# In run_infomap()
import os
os.makedirs("out", exist_ok=True)

# In infomap_communities()  
edgelist_dir = os.path.dirname(edgelist_file)
if edgelist_dir:
    os.makedirs(edgelist_dir, exist_ok=True)
```

## Testing Infrastructure

Added comprehensive testing infrastructure to ensure the fix works and prevent future regressions:

- **`test_infomap_fix.py`**: Integration test that verifies the complete infomap workflow including directory creation, binary execution, and output file parsing
- **`run_tests.py`**: Robust test runner with dependency handling and clear output formatting
- **`TESTING.md`**: Documentation explaining how to run tests and handle dependencies

The test runner gracefully handles missing dependencies and provides clear instructions for installation.

## Test Results

```bash
python run_tests.py
```

- ✅ **test_infomap_fix.py**: Passes - verifies the fix works end-to-end with actual infomap binary
- ⚠️ **test_core_functionality.py**: Requires visualization dependencies (matplotlib, etc.)

This minimal change (3 lines added) resolves the critical issue preventing infomap community detection from working in clean environments, while adding robust testing to prevent future regressions.

Fixes #24.

author: therandomstring
body:
<!--
Thank you for contributing to syslog-ng. Please make sure you:
- Read our Contribution guideline: https://github.com/syslog-ng/syslog-ng/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md
- Checked that tests pass (including stylechecks: `make style-check`)
- Wrote a news file, if applicable: https://github.com/syslog-ng/syslog-ng/tree/master/news
-->
This PR contains general compatibility improvements to ease inclusion into AIX Toolbox for Open Source Software.

## COMPILATION
(Taken from #5469)

### Env:

Currently, the used account has (almost) all the required settings in its `.profile`, but a usable setup can be:

```
#
# AIX 7.2
#
# Location of the system packages (added via `dnf install`)
# By default, it is /opt/freeware
export SYSPKG_PREFIX=/opt/freeware
export SYSPKG_REPOSITORY=${SYSPKG_PREFIX}

# Location of the user built packages (added via custom user builds and installs)
# By default, it is /usr/local
export USRPKG_PREFIX=/usr/local
export USRPKG_REPOSITORY=${USRPKG_PREFIX}

# By a good chance, for both of the above installations, these are already added, but
# if you don't, you will need it to get the pkgconfig mechanism working
#export PATH=${SYSPKG_PREFIX}/bin:${SYSPKG_PREFIX}/sbin:${PATH}

# These are also required to get the pkgconfig work 
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="${SYSPKG_PREFIX}/lib/pkgconfig:${USRPKG_PREFIX}/lib/pkgconfig:${PKG_CONFIG_PATH}"


# Normally, you do not need this, add it if pkgconfig cannot find the headers of the system or user installed packages from the info stored in the pkgconfig files
#export CFLAGS="-I${SYSPKG_PREFIX}/include/ -I${USRPKG_PREFIX}/include/ ${CFLAGS}"
#export CPPFLAGS="${CFLAGS} ${CPPFLAGS}"


# Normally, you do not need this, add it if pkgconfig cannot find the libraries of the system or user installed packages from the info stored in the pkgconfig files
# Currenty the libSNMP package is the only one that requires this, so use it
# TODO: Add FindlibSNMP.cmake to correct the broken pkginfo file of it
export LDFLAGS="-L${SYSPKG_PREFIX}/lib -L${USRPKG_PREFIX}/lib ${LDFLAGS}"

# These are needed for proper threading support linking
export LDFLAGS="${LDFLAGS} -lthread -lpthreads -lbsd"

```

### Build:

```
# Configure
# NOTE: if you have newer than 3.11 python installed you might want to add -DENABLE_PYTHON_MODULES=OFF -DENABLE_PYTHON=OFF as well

cmake --install-prefix build/install -B build . -DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=OFF -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -DIVYKIS_SOURCE=internal -DENABLE_EXTRA_WARNINGS=ON -DENABLE_MANPAGES=ON -DCMAKE_VERBOSE_MAKEFILE=OFF -DENABLE_CPP=OFF -DENABLE_JAVA=OFF -DENABLE_JAVA_MODULES=OFF -DBUILD_TESTING=OFF -DENABLE_FORCE_GNU99=ON -DSUMMARY_LEVEL=0 -Werror -Wno-dev --fresh

# Make

cmake --build ./build --target install -j$(( $(nproc) > 1 ? $(nproc) - 1 : 1 ))
```

### Test:

```
LIBPATH=${USRPKG_PREFIX}/lib:${LIBPATH} build/install/sbin/syslog-ng -V
```

author: jenkoian
body:
Text field has a length of 65,535 characters which can easily be reached if triggering a backfill with lots of partitions.

This changes the column type to mediumtext which has a character limit of 16,777,215 characters which should be ample (don't think we need to go to longtext just yet).

Sqlite and Postgres do not have a length limit on text, so this will only apply to Mysql.

## Summary & Motivation

Runs page wouldn't load without error, see https://github.com/dagster-io/dagster/issues/31540

Closes #31540

I could do with some help with this, I've not really tested it and not quite sure how to.

Added migration to alter bulk_actions.body column from text to mediumtext for Mysql storage
